modules.title: Huntsman — Depreciation And Amoritization Schedule
modules.description: Rebuild each block in the same order as the workbook, then defend its links, signs, and forecast mechanics.

questions.question: Why is Capex % Revenue shown as a negative assumption in this schedule?
options: Because capex is a cash outflow on the investing section of the CFS
Because gross PP&E must decline whenever the company invests
Because depreciation is recorded as a positive asset
Because the tax rate is applied to capex
questions.explanation: The schedule stores capex using the CFS sign convention: a cash investment is negative.

questions.question: How is forecast PP&E depreciation calculated in this model?
options: Ending net PP&E multiplied by the tax rate
Average gross PP&E multiplied by the depreciation rate
Revenue multiplied by the amortization rate
questions.explanation: The depreciation rate is applied to the average gross PP&E balance for the year.

questions.question: Forecast PP/E FX and the forecast disposal / other rows are zero. What does that assumption mean?
options: The model assumes no specific forecast FX, disposal, or reclassification activity
The model assumes PP&E has no value
The model assumes capex is zero
The model assumes accumulated depreciation is written off
questions.explanation: The historical rows explain reported movements; the forecast starts at zero absent a supported event.

questions.question: What supports the forecast existing-intangible amortization amounts through 2030?
questions.explanation: The forecast uses the disclosed future amortization schedule; 2031 is an analyst carry-forward assumption.

questions.question: What should Beginning Gross PP&E equal in each forecast year?
questions.explanation: The asset balance rolls forward from the prior year's ending gross PP&E.

questions.question: With capital expenditures stored as a negative number, which formula is correct?
options: Ending Gross PP&E = Beginning Gross PP&E + Capex + Assets/Other
Ending Gross PP&E = Beginning Gross PP&E - Capex + Assets/Other
Ending Gross PP&E = Beginning Gross PP&E - Depreciation
Ending Gross PP&E = Net PP&E + Total D&A
questions.explanation: Subtracting negative capex adds the investment to gross PP&E.

questions.question: Where should the Capital Expenditures row link?
questions.explanation: The same capex assumption drives the PP&E roll-forward and investing cash flow.

questions.question: What does historical Assets/Other (plug) explain?
options: Disposals, FX, divestitures, and reclassifications not separately available
The difference between basic and diluted shares
questions.explanation: It reconciles changes in gross PP&E that are not explained by capex alone.

questions.question: Accumulated depreciation is shown as a negative balance. Which forecast formula is correct?
options: Ending AD = Beginning AD - Depreciation + Disposals/Other
Ending AD = Beginning AD + Depreciation + Capex
Ending AD = Gross PP&E - Net Income
Ending AD = Beginning AD + Total D&A
questions.explanation: A positive depreciation expense makes the negative contra-asset more negative.

questions.question: How is Net PP&E calculated in this schedule?
options: Ending Gross PP&E plus Ending Accumulated Depreciation
Ending Gross PP&E plus capital expenditures
questions.explanation: Because accumulated depreciation is negative, it is added to gross PP&E to produce net PP&E.

questions.question: Where should forecast Net PP&E flow?
options: The standalone balance-sheet Net PP&E line
questions.explanation: The D&A schedule owns the forecast PP&E balance and feeds the balance sheet.

questions.question: If depreciation is already embedded in COGS or other operating expenses, how should the model use this depreciation row?
options: Add it as a second operating expense
Use it for the PP&E roll-forward, CFO add-back, and EBITDA memo without double counting it on the IS
questions.explanation: The schedule supports D&A and asset balances, but an extra IS expense would double count embedded depreciation.

questions.question: With no forecast additions, which intangible roll-forward is correct?
options: Ending Net Intangibles = Beginning Net Intangibles - Amortization Expense
Ending Net Intangibles = Beginning Net Intangibles + Amortization Expense
questions.explanation: Amortization reduces the existing finite-lived intangible balance.

questions.question: Where should Ending Net Intangibles flow?
options: The standalone balance-sheet Intangible Assets line
questions.explanation: The existing-intangible schedule owns the forecast intangible-asset balance.

questions.question: Where does Amortization Expense also appear?
options: As part of the CFS D&A add-back and Total D&A
questions.explanation: It is a noncash expense included in the D&A bridge.

questions.question: Should this legacy amortization be driven by the future PPA intangible-life assumption?
options: Yes, because all intangible assets are transaction assets
No; legacy amortization and incremental PPA amortization are separate systems
Yes, because PPA replaces the standalone model
No, because amortization never affects earnings
questions.explanation: This block covers Huntsman's existing intangibles; new transaction intangibles belong in the PPA schedule.

questions.question: How is Total D&A calculated here?
options: PP&E Depreciation plus Existing Intangible Amortization
questions.explanation: The standalone D&A total combines legacy PP&E depreciation and legacy intangible amortization.

questions.question: Where should Total D&A link in the standalone model?
options: The CFS noncash add-back and the EBITDA memo calculation
Only the financing section of the CFS
questions.explanation: Total D&A supports cash flow and EBITDA while the asset schedules support the balance sheet.

questions.question: Which item should not be included in this Total D&A line?
questions.explanation: Debt issuance-cost amortization is a financing expense, not depreciation or amortization of operating assets.

questions.question: What will the pro forma D&A schedule add later?
options: Olin legacy D&A, Huntsman legacy D&A, and incremental PPA depreciation / amortization
questions.explanation: The consolidated company combines both legacy asset bases with purchase-accounting adjustments.

modules.title: Olin — Share Schedule
modules.description: Rebuild the share and equity roll-forwards, then defend the units, linkage direction, and accounting treatment.

questions.question: What unit does Net Shares Issued / Repurchaed use?
questions.explanation: It is a share-count movement, not a cash-flow dollar amount.

questions.question: How is historical Past Dilutive Effect calculated from Mergent data?
options: Diluted weighted-average shares less basic weighted-average shares
Stock compensation divided by share price
Net income divided by diluted EPS
questions.explanation: The difference between diluted and basic weighted-average shares is the historical incremental dilution included in EPS.

questions.question: Why should Stock Compensation not be subtracted from the dilutive-share assumption?
options: They use different units: dollars versus shares
Stock compensation is a debt balance
Stock compensation is a cash dividend
questions.explanation: Converting expense into shares would require grants, vesting, exercise prices, forfeitures, and share-price assumptions.

questions.question: Why are Other Equity Changes and Other Retained Earnings Adjustments zero in forecast?
options: No recurring forecast adjustment is supported
They are already included in debt
questions.explanation: Historical residual movements are not projected without a specific assumption.

questions.question: Which ending-share formula is correct?
options: Ending Common Shares = Beginning Common Shares + Net Shares Issued / (Repurchased)
Ending Common Shares = Beginning Common Shares + Dividends Paid
Ending Common Shares = Diluted EPS × Net Income
Ending Common Shares = APIC - Treasury Stock
questions.explanation: The share-count roll-forward is driven by actual issuance and repurchase activity.

questions.question: What does AVERAGE(Beginning Shares, Ending Shares) assume?
options: The net share change occurs halfway through the year
All shares are issued on December 31
questions.explanation: It is a simplified time-weighting convention for the basic denominator.

questions.question: How is Weighted-Average Diluted Shares calculated in this simplified schedule?
options: Weighted-Average Common Shares plus Dilutive Effect
Ending Common Shares plus Common Stock
Net Income divided by share price
questions.explanation: The incremental diluted-share effect is added to the weighted-average basic/common shares.

questions.question: Which share row should feed the standalone EPS denominator?
questions.explanation: EPS uses the period-average diluted denominator, not a year-end point-in-time count.

questions.question: Should the approximately 97.5mm merger consideration shares enter this standalone schedule?
options: No; they belong in the transaction / pro forma share-count schedule
Yes; add them to every forecast year
Yes; add them to historical diluted shares
No; because merger shares never affect EPS
questions.explanation: Standalone Olin excludes transaction-specific issuance until the pro forma model.

questions.question: Which formula is the cleanest annual dividend convention?
options: Dividends Paid = -Dividend Per Share × Weighted-Average Common Shares
Dividends Paid = Dividend Per Share × Ending Debt
questions.explanation: The negative sign reflects a financing cash outflow and a reduction to retained earnings.

questions.question: Where does Dividends Paid flow?
options: Financing cash flow and the retained-earnings roll-forward
questions.explanation: Dividends reduce cash through CFF and reduce retained earnings.

questions.question: Why should Dividends Paid not reduce APIC?
options: Ordinary dividends are distributions of retained earnings, not contributed capital
questions.explanation: APIC records contributed capital and certain equity-compensation effects, not ordinary dividend distributions.

blocks.title: Common Stock, APIC, and Treasury Stock

questions.question: What does the Common Stock balance represent?
options: The par-value component of issued shares
questions.explanation: Common Stock is a dollar equity account based on par value, not market price.

questions.question: In the simplified noncash employee-share issuance, how should the $20mm stock-compensation equity credit be allocated?
options: Common Stock receives par value and APIC receives the remainder
Treasury Stock receives the full amount
Retained Earnings receives the full amount
questions.explanation: The total equity credit must be split without double counting Common Stock and APIC.

questions.question: Why is stock-based compensation added back in CFO?
options: It reduced earnings but did not use current-period cash
questions.explanation: The expense is noncash in the period and typically increases APIC.

questions.question: When should Treasury Stock change?
options: When shares are repurchased into treasury or treasury shares are reissued
questions.explanation: A share-count change alone does not prove the Treasury Stock dollar balance moved.

questions.question: What double-counting error occurs if Common Stock rises by par value and the full stock-compensation credit is also added to APIC?
options: Total equity is overstated by the Common Stock increase
Cash is understated by the full compensation expense
Debt is overstated by par value
questions.explanation: The total equity credit should be divided between Common Stock and APIC, not recorded in both.

questions.question: Which retained-earnings formula is correct when Dividends Paid is already negative?
options: Ending RE = Beginning RE + Net Income + Dividends Paid + Other Adjustments
Ending RE = Beginning RE + Net Income - Dividends Paid
questions.explanation: Adding the signed negative dividend amount reduces retained earnings.

questions.question: What should Beginning Retained Earnings equal after the first year?
questions.explanation: Retained earnings is a cumulative balance that rolls forward year to year.

questions.question: Where should forecast Net Income in this schedule come from?
questions.explanation: The equity schedule links the earnings generated by the standalone model.

questions.question: Why is Other Retained Earnigns Adjustments zero in forecast?
options: No recurring direct retained-earnings adjustment is supported
questions.explanation: Historical residual adjustments are not automatically projected.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Total Equity?
options: Common Stock + APIC + Treasury Stock + Ending Retained Earnings + Other Equity
questions.explanation: All equity components are summed using their displayed signs.

questions.question: Should Stock-Based Compensation be added again in Total Equity after it has already rolled into APIC?
options: No; that would double count the equity credit
Yes; it must be added to every equity line
Yes; but only in loss years
No; because stock compensation is debt
questions.explanation: Total Equity uses ending account balances, not every movement row.

questions.question: Should Other Retained Earnings Adjustments be added again after Ending Retained Earnings already includes them?
options: No; that would double count the adjustment
Yes; it is always a separate equity account
No; because retained earnings is a liability
questions.explanation: The adjustment is a roll-forward component, not an additional ending equity account.

questions.question: Where should Total Equity flow?
options: The Olin standalone balance-sheet Total Equity line
The Sources & Uses share issuance detail
questions.explanation: The equity schedule owns forecast shareholder-equity balances.

questions.question: What does Positive Share Toggle = 1 mean?
options: Positive share changes are treated as newly issued shares
Positive share changes are treated as debt
questions.explanation: New issuance affects Common Stock by par value and APIC by the remaining equity credit or proceeds.

questions.question: What does Positive Share Toggle = 0 mean?
options: Treasury shares are reissued rather than newly issued
questions.explanation: A treasury-share reissuance generally leaves Common Stock unchanged and reduces the contra-equity balance.

questions.question: What does Negative Share Treatment = 1 mean?
options: Repurchased shares are held in treasury
questions.explanation: Retirement reduces Common Stock by par value and allocates the remaining cost to APIC / retained earnings.

questions.question: What does Negative Share Treatment = 0 mean?
options: Repurchased shares are held in treasury
questions.explanation: The repurchase cost is recorded in Treasury Stock as a negative equity balance.

questions.question: Why is Par Value Per Share not enough to calculate Treasury Stock?
options: Treasury Stock is recorded at repurchase cost, so a dollar cash amount or cost basis is also needed
Treasury Stock is measured only in shares
questions.explanation: Par value determines the Common Stock component; treasury accounting requires the actual cost basis.

modules.title: PPA & Goodwill
modules.description: Rebuild purchase consideration, the goodwill bridge, and transaction-date-driven incremental PPA D&A.

questions.question: Which formula should calculate Total Purchase Consideration?
options: Value of Shares Issued + Financing Fees
questions.explanation: Purchase consideration includes consideration transferred, not enterprise value or deal fees.

questions.question: Why is target net debt excluded from Total Purchase Consideration for goodwill?
options: Net debt is part of enterprise value, not additional consideration transferred for the target equity.
Target debt is always written off at close.
Debt never affects a merger model.
Net debt is already included in transaction fees.
questions.explanation: The PPA begins with consideration transferred; enterprise value is a valuation bridge.

questions.question: How should transaction fees enter this block?
options: Add them only when the deal is all stock.
Add them to Other Purchase Consideration.
Subtract them from target book equity.
They should not enter purchase consideration or goodwill.
questions.explanation: Transaction fees are expensed separately and are not consideration transferred.

questions.question: Where should Equity Consideration and Other Purchase Consideration normally link from?
questions.explanation: The transaction assumptions page owns the deal consideration inputs.

questions.question: Why are Existing Goodwill and Existing Intangibles added back after subtracting Target Book Equity?
options: They are embedded in book equity but are eliminated or remeasured in purchase accounting.
They are cash sources at close.
questions.explanation: The bridge removes book net assets and rebuilds identifiable net assets at fair value.

questions.question: Which simplified goodwill formula is correct?
options: Purchase Consideration - Target Book Equity + Existing Goodwill + Existing Intangibles - PP&E Step-Up - New Intangibles + New Liabilities + Incremental DTL + Other Adjustments
Purchase Consideration + Target Book Equity - Existing Goodwill - Existing Intangibles
Enterprise Value - Target Debt + Transaction Fees
questions.explanation: The signs reflect the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired.

questions.question: What should the deferred-tax line represent?
options: Only the incremental tax effect of the PPA fair-value adjustments
The target's entire existing deferred-tax balance again
questions.explanation: Existing deferred taxes are already included in target book net assets.

questions.question: Which PPA items are normally blue user inputs when no preliminary allocation is disclosed?
options: PP&E Step-Up, New Identifiable Intangibles, New Identifiable Liabilities, and Other Fair Value Adjustments
Target Book Equity and Existing Goodwill
Equity Consideration and Target Diluted Shares
questions.explanation: Fair-value estimates require explicit assumptions unless the filing supplies them.

questions.question: Where should New Goodwill flow after it is calculated?
options: The Purchase Accounting Adjustments column of the pro forma opening balance sheet
questions.explanation: New goodwill is a day-one purchase-accounting asset.

questions.question: What should 2026E incremental PPA D&A equal for a June 30, 2027 close?
questions.explanation: Purchase-accounting expense begins only after the transaction closes.

questions.question: How should the 2027 closing-year expense be calculated?
options: Annual expense multiplied by the post-close fraction of 2027
Annual expense multiplied by the pre-close fraction
A full annual expense regardless of close date
questions.explanation: A date-driven stub convention captures the period from close through year-end.

questions.question: Which assumptions should drive the two annual expense rows?
options: Debt Maturity and Target Net Debt
PP&E Step-Up Life for depreciation and Intangible Amortization Life for amortization
questions.explanation: The step-up amounts are divided by their respective useful lives.

questions.question: Why should Total Incremental D&A not be added to the standalone schedules?
options: It is a cash use in Sources & Uses.
It is already included in target debt.
It is transaction-created expense that belongs in the pro forma consolidation.
questions.explanation: Standalone schedules must remain valid on a no-deal basis.

questions.question: Which formula should calculate Total Incremental D&A?
questions.explanation: The total combines the two purchase-accounting noncash expense streams.

questions.question: What should Huntsman Standalone contribute to the PPA tab?
options: Target book equity, existing goodwill, and existing intangibles at the selected pre-close date
New debt issued and financing fees
questions.explanation: The target standalone supplies the book balances being acquired.

questions.question: Which schedule should own the PP&E step-up amount and new identifiable-intangible amount?
questions.explanation: The PPA schedule owns fair-value allocation amounts.

questions.question: Where do the new goodwill and day-one asset/liability adjustments flow first?
questions.explanation: The opening balance sheet records the acquisition accounting at close.

questions.question: Where does incremental PPA D&A flow after the PPA tab?
options: Pro Forma D&A and then the consolidated statements
Back into the target standalone D&A schedule
questions.explanation: The pro forma D&A bridge carries transaction-created expense into consolidation.

modules.title: Transaction & Refinancing Debt
modules.description: Rebuild the joint close-date debt bridge from standalone balances through repayment, remaining debt, new financing, fees, and interest.

questions.question: What should Closing Balance link to?
options: The debt table's original 2025 balance in every case
The instrument's ending balance at the latest pre-close year-end in its standalone debt schedule
questions.explanation: Standalone debt schedules remain the source of truth for pre-close balances.

questions.question: Which formula calculates Debt Repaid / Refinanced?
options: Closing Balance × Instrument Toggle × Global Close Debt Treatment Switch
questions.explanation: Both the instrument selection and the global scenario switch must be active.

questions.question: Which formula calculates Debt Remaining?
options: Closing Balance × Pro Forma Interest Rate
questions.explanation: The joint tab separates extinguished debt from debt that survives closing.

questions.question: When should Pro Forma Interest Rate equal zero?
options: Whenever the instrument toggle is zero
Whenever the close date is midyear
questions.explanation: A fully repaid instrument should contribute no post-close interest.

questions.question: What should Pro Forma Interest Expense equal for remaining existing debt in the simple opening calculation?
questions.explanation: The current joint tab uses the surviving principal and rate for a simple annual interest estimate.

questions.question: Which summary should feed Acquirer Debt Repaid / Refinanced in Sources & Uses?
questions.explanation: The acquirer parent row should link to the acquirer's selected extinguishments.

questions.question: Which summary should feed Target Debt Repaid / Refinanced in Sources & Uses?
questions.explanation: The target parent row should link to the target's selected extinguishments.

questions.question: How is Total Existing Debt Remaining calculated?
options: Olin Debt Repaid + Huntsman Debt Repaid
Olin Debt Remaining + Huntsman Debt Remaining
Total Debt Repaid + Total New Debt Issued
questions.explanation: It is the surviving pre-close debt before adding any new financing.

questions.question: Why should Total Existing Interest Expense be kept separate from new-debt interest?
options: The consolidated interest build must distinguish surviving legacy debt from newly issued financing.
Existing interest is a purchase-accounting asset.
The two rates must always be identical.
questions.explanation: Separate components make the post-close interest bridge auditable.

questions.question: Which formula calculates Amount Issued?
options: Base Amount × Close Debt Treatment Switch
questions.explanation: The new-debt scenario is controlled by its own global switch.

questions.question: Should the existing-debt close-treatment switch control new debt issuance?
options: Yes; otherwise Sources & Uses cannot balance.
Yes; both switches should always be identical.
No; new debt should ignore every switch.
No; the Debt Financing Switch controls new debt.
questions.explanation: Repaying old debt and issuing new debt are separate decisions.

questions.question: How should an aggregate financing-fee input be handled across multiple active tranches?
options: Allocate it across all base amounts even when the switch is off.
Apply the full fee to every tranche.
Ignore it until consolidated statements are built.
Allocate it across active Amount Issued balances, or use another explicit allocation assumption.
questions.explanation: The allocated tranche fees must sum to the aggregate financing-fee input.

questions.question: Which formula calculates simple annual new-debt interest?
questions.explanation: Only debt actually issued contributes new-debt interest.

questions.question: Why must Financing Fees remain wired when the current input is zero?
options: The workbook is a reusable template and must work when a future scenario turns the fee input on.
Financing fees never affect the balance sheet.
Zero inputs should always be deleted.
questions.explanation: A zero current case is not a reason to omit required template mechanics.

questions.question: How is Total Pro Forma Debt calculated at close?
options: Total Debt Repaid + Total Financing Fees
Total Existing Debt Remaining + Total New Debt Issued
questions.explanation: The pro forma capital structure contains surviving legacy debt plus new financing.

questions.question: Which new-debt summary should feed Sources & Uses?
questions.explanation: Sources & Uses records the gross new borrowing source, not all debt outstanding.

questions.question: Which fee summary should feed the Sources & Uses financing-fee use?
questions.explanation: The aggregate fee output is the closing cash use and day-one contra-debt amount.

questions.question: Why should the row be called Total New Debt Interest Expense rather than Total Pro Forma Interest Expense?
options: All existing debt is automatically repaid.
Interest expense is not part of the model.
It includes only new-debt interest; surviving existing-debt interest is summarized separately.
The row includes transaction fees instead.
questions.explanation: Clear labels prevent the consolidated interest build from omitting or double counting legacy interest.

questions.question: Why should the joint debt tab not recreate custom-loan or revolver mechanics?
options: Custom debt is ignored after signing.
Sources & Uses owns all forecast debt.
The pro forma balance sheet should hardcode them.
Those mechanics already belong to the standalone debt schedules.
questions.explanation: Duplicating the logic would create conflicting sources of truth.

questions.question: What does the joint debt tab decide?
options: Which pre-close balances are repaid or remain, plus what new debt is issued
questions.explanation: It is the transaction bridge between standalone debt and the combined capital structure.

questions.question: Why should Sources & Uses link from the joint tab?
options: The joint tab is only a formatting sheet.
The joint tab already applies close treatment and new-financing logic.
Sources & Uses should calculate every standalone debt balance.
questions.explanation: This preserves schedule ownership and keeps deal funding auditable.

questions.question: Where should post-close interest ultimately be calculated?
options: A consolidated interest build using surviving existing debt, new debt, and fee amortization
questions.explanation: The combined company needs a distinct post-close interest calculation.

modules.title: Sources & Uses — Joint Debt Flow
modules.description: Rebuild Sources & Uses after rerouting existing debt, new debt, and financing fees through the joint refinancing schedule.

blocks.title: Uses of Funds
rows: Target Debt Repaid / Refinanced at Close
Acquirer Debt Repaid / Refinanced at Close

questions.question: Which debt amounts should appear as Uses?
options: Gross target and acquirer debt actually repaid or refinanced at close
All target and acquirer debt outstanding
Only the net change in debt
questions.explanation: Old principal extinguished at close is a use of funds.

questions.question: Should Other Purchase Consideration automatically appear as Other Cash Consideration?
options: Yes; purchase consideration and cash consideration are identical.
No; only the portion that is actually a closing cash payment belongs in Sources & Uses.
No; other consideration never affects goodwill.
Yes; every PPA item is a cash use.
questions.explanation: Purchase-accounting consideration and closing cash funding are related but not automatically identical.

questions.question: Where do financing fees appear?
options: As a separate use linked from the joint debt schedule
questions.explanation: Debt financing costs are distinct from transaction fees and principal repayment.

questions.question: How should Total Uses be calculated?
options: Set it equal to enterprise value.
Use Total Sources as a plug.
Sum every parent and every detail row together.
Sum the parent use lines without double counting their inserted detail rows.
questions.explanation: Detail rows support the parent subtotals; they should not be counted again in the grand total.

questions.question: What should Value of Shares Issued equal in an all-stock transaction?
options: Target diluted shares × target share price only
New consideration shares × acquirer reference share price
questions.explanation: This is the equity funding source for the share consideration.

questions.question: How should Existing Cash Used behave?
options: It should become negative when the deal is overfunded.
It should equal total target cash.
It should plug only the remaining real cash requirement and be bounded at zero.
It should always equal transaction fees.
questions.explanation: Negative cash used is not an economic funding source.

questions.question: What should New Debt Issued link to?
options: Total New Debt Issued from the joint debt tab
questions.explanation: Sources & Uses records only the new borrowing raised for the transaction.

questions.question: What must Sources - Uses equal?
questions.explanation: A balanced Sources & Uses proves every use has a funding source.

questions.question: What is the role of the individual close-treatment toggle?
options: It selects whether a specific existing instrument is extinguished at close.
questions.explanation: Instrument-level selection belongs to the existing debt treatment table.

questions.question: What is the role of the global Close Debt Treatment Switch?
options: It activates or deactivates the selected existing-debt repayments as a scenario.
questions.explanation: The global switch turns the entire close-debt scenario on or off.

questions.question: What is the role of the Debt Financing Switch?
options: It activates or deactivates new debt issuance.
questions.explanation: New financing and existing debt treatment are separate scenario levers.

questions.question: If all existing-debt toggles are zero but the new-debt switch is one, what happens?
options: Half of every debt balance is refinanced.
No existing debt is repaid, but selected new debt is still issued.
No new debt can be issued.
questions.explanation: The two switch systems operate independently.

questions.question: After the joint debt tab is built, where should the macro read debt amounts?
options: Directly from the standalone debt buildouts
The pro forma opening balance sheet
questions.explanation: The joint tab owns the close treatment and new-financing outputs.

questions.question: What should the macro do?
options: Insert or delete detail rows and create live links to the joint debt tab.
Calculate closing balances and interest from scratch.
questions.explanation: The macro manages presentation structure, not core debt mechanics.

questions.question: When is a refresh required?
options: After instruments are added, deleted, renamed, or the table structure changes
questions.explanation: Live formulas handle ordinary amount and switch changes.

questions.question: Why should macro-generated formula text be black in this workbook?
options: The user chose black formula formatting and rejected green linked-text formatting.
questions.explanation: The macro should preserve the workbook's selected presentation convention.

modules.title: Pro Forma Opening Balance Sheet
modules.description: Rebuild the day-one balance-sheet bridge, classify purchase-accounting and transaction adjustments, and defend every subtotal and check.

questions.question: Which formula should calculate an ordinary Pro Forma Opening line?
options: Olin + Huntsman + Purchase Accounting Adjustments + Transaction Adjustments
questions.explanation: The opening balance combines both companies and both adjustment categories.

questions.question: What do the Olin and Huntsman columns represent?
options: The latest pre-close annual balance-sheet proxy for each standalone company
Only historical 2025 balances regardless of close date
questions.explanation: The annual model dynamically selects the latest fiscal year-end before close.

questions.question: Why keep Purchase Accounting and Transaction Adjustments separate?
options: The balance sheet cannot sum one adjustment column.
They distinguish fair-value and equity-elimination entries from funding and closing mechanics.
One is for assets and one is for liabilities only.
questions.explanation: The separation makes the day-one bridge easier to audit.

questions.question: What date does Pro Forma Opening conceptually represent?
questions.explanation: It is the combined company's day-one balance sheet.

questions.question: Which current-asset row normally receives the main transaction adjustment?
questions.explanation: Existing cash used and any explicit excess-cash treatment affect opening cash.

questions.question: Should Accounts Receivable and Inventory change automatically just because the merger closes?
options: No; leave them unchanged unless a specific fair-value adjustment is modeled.
Yes; add transaction fees to both.
No; exclude the target balances entirely.
questions.explanation: Only supported purchase-accounting adjustments should change operating assets.

questions.question: How should Total Current Assets be calculated?
options: Sum the adjusted Pro Forma Opening current-asset lines
Use Total Assets less Net PP&E
Sum the two standalone Total Current Assets rows only
questions.explanation: The subtotal must include transaction adjustments to the component rows.

questions.question: What happens to cash when Existing Cash Used is zero because the deal is overfunded?
options: Cash should be set to zero.
The Existing Cash Used adjustment is zero; the financing surplus must be resolved elsewhere.
Cash should be reduced by the negative plug.
questions.explanation: A bounded cash-use formula cannot absorb excess financing.

questions.question: Where should the PP&E step-up be recorded on day one?
options: Gross PP&E, with no opening accumulated depreciation on the new step-up
questions.explanation: The fair-value increment starts as a new gross asset basis.

questions.question: How is the Goodwill adjustment calculated?
questions.explanation: Target historical goodwill is eliminated and replaced by acquisition-date goodwill.

questions.question: How is the Intangible Assets adjustment calculated?
options: Add both historical and new intangibles without elimination
questions.explanation: The target's old carrying value is replaced by the new fair-value amount.

questions.question: How should Net PP&E be calculated?
questions.explanation: Accumulated depreciation is displayed as a negative contra-asset.

questions.question: How should Total Assets be calculated?
options: Olin Total Assets + Huntsman Total Assets only
Total Current Assets plus all adjusted noncurrent asset lines
questions.explanation: The subtotal must be rebuilt from the pro forma component balances.

questions.question: Which current-liability row receives the selected current debt repayment adjustment?
questions.explanation: Debt due within the selected current-classification window is removed from current debt.

questions.question: Should Accounts Payable or Accrued Expenses be eliminated with target equity?
options: No; they are acquired liabilities and remain unless specifically remeasured.
Yes; every target liability is eliminated.
questions.explanation: Purchase accounting remeasures liabilities; it does not erase ordinary obligations.

questions.question: How should Total Current Liabilities be calculated?
options: Set it equal to current assets
Use Olin Total Current Liabilities only
Sum the adjusted Pro Forma Opening current-liability lines
Sum the two standalone subtotal rows without adjustment
questions.explanation: The subtotal must capture the debt transaction adjustment.

questions.question: Why can a debt instrument's current-versus-long-term classification change by transaction date?
options: The exchange ratio changes its maturity.
The classification depends on the latest pre-close year-end and whether maturity is within the next twelve months.
questions.explanation: Debt classification is date-dependent even when principal is unchanged.

questions.question: How is the Long-Term Debt transaction adjustment calculated in the current simplified setup?
options: -Total Debt Repaid with no new debt
-Long-Term Debt Repaid + New Long-Term Debt Issued
questions.explanation: The adjustment removes selected long-term principal and adds new long-term financing.

questions.question: How do new financing fees affect Less: Debt Issuance Costs?
options: They make the contra-liability more negative, net of any old costs written off.
They increase Long-Term Debt principal directly.
questions.explanation: Capitalized financing costs reduce the carrying amount of debt.

questions.question: Where should the incremental PPA DTL flow?
options: Deferred Taxes in Purchase Accounting Adjustments
questions.explanation: The DTL is created by acquisition-date book-tax basis differences.

questions.question: Where should New Identifiable Liabilities flow?
options: Other Long-Term Liabilities in Purchase Accounting Adjustments, unless a more specific row exists
questions.explanation: The generic row is the current template location for new non-debt PPA liabilities.

questions.question: How should Total Liabilities be calculated?
options: Olin Total Liabilities + Huntsman Total Liabilities only
Total Current Liabilities + Total Long-Term Debt + Deferred Taxes + Other Long-Term Liabilities + NCI
questions.explanation: The subtotal must use adjusted pro forma liability balances.

questions.question: What happens to Huntsman's historical equity accounts in purchase accounting?
options: Only Huntsman Common Stock is eliminated.
questions.explanation: The acquirer does not carry forward the target's historical shareholder-equity accounts.

questions.question: How is the new Olin Common Stock adjustment calculated?
options: Value of shares issued at market value
New consideration shares × Olin par value per share
questions.explanation: Common Stock records only the par-value portion of the new shares.

questions.question: How is the new Olin APIC adjustment calculated?
options: Value of shares issued - Common Stock adjustment
Value of shares issued + Common Stock adjustment
questions.explanation: The market-value equity issuance is split between par value and APIC.

questions.question: Which fee should reduce opening retained earnings?
options: Transaction fees that are expensed at close
questions.explanation: Transaction expenses reduce earnings/equity; financing fees are capitalized against debt.

questions.question: Which formula calculates the final balance-sheet check?
options: Total Assets - Total Liabilities and Equity
questions.explanation: The opening balance sheet must balance after every adjustment.

questions.question: Which of these is a Purchase Accounting Adjustment rather than a Transaction Adjustment?
questions.explanation: The step-up remeasures the acquired asset at fair value.

questions.question: Which of these is a Transaction Adjustment rather than a Purchase Accounting Adjustment?
questions.explanation: New borrowing is a funding mechanic, not a fair-value allocation.

questions.question: Why is Target Equity Elimination grouped with purchase accounting?
options: The acquired company's historical equity does not survive consolidation.
questions.explanation: Purchase accounting replaces the target's historical equity with the acquirer's consideration and acquired net assets.

questions.question: Why do Transaction Fees and Financing Fees go to different balance-sheet rows?
options: Transaction fees reduce earnings/equity, while financing fees create a contra-debt asset or reduction to debt carrying value.
questions.explanation: The accounting follows the nature of the cost.

questions.question: What is the danger of calculating Pro Forma Opening by summing standalone subtotal rows?
options: It can omit line-item adjustments and still produce a misleading zero check.
It makes goodwill negative by definition.
It prevents formulas from copying down.
It always double counts cash only.
questions.explanation: Every subtotal must be recomputed from adjusted pro forma components.

modules.title: Pro Forma D&A
modules.description: Rebuild the close-timed depreciation and amortization bridge without double-counting legacy D&A.

questions.question: Why is Post-Close Period zero before the close year?
options: The transaction has not occurred, so target and PPA D&A are excluded.
The target has no fixed assets.
The model uses full-year pro forma results in every column.
questions.explanation: The consolidated forecast follows the actual assumed close date.

questions.question: Which useful-life links are correct?
questions.explanation: J20 and J23 are the actual useful-life assumptions.

questions.question: What does repeating the $200mm intangible assumption across post-close columns mean?
options: The same close-date asset is displayed for reference.
A new $200mm asset is acquired every year.
questions.explanation: Only the expense repeats; the asset is recognized once.

questions.question: Why include 2025A in the schedule?
options: It provides a historical anchor and lets timing formulas zero out irrelevant periods.
questions.explanation: The anchor improves traceability and template reusability.

questions.question: How is Post-Close Huntsman Depreciation calculated?
questions.explanation: Target flow items are stubbed from the close date.

questions.question: How is incremental step-up depreciation calculated?
questions.explanation: The close-year amount is a straight-line annual expense multiplied by the stub.

questions.question: What is full-year depreciation on a $100mm step-up with a 10-year life?
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation is $100mm / 10.

questions.question: What is Pro Forma Depreciation?
options: Olin full-year + post-close Huntsman + incremental step-up depreciation
Full Olin + full Huntsman in every year
questions.explanation: The bridge follows the actual close date.

questions.question: Why is target legacy amortization eliminated?
options: PPA removes the old target intangible balance and replaces it with newly valued identifiable intangibles.
The target has no historical intangibles.
questions.explanation: The old carrying-value expense does not survive the purchase-accounting reset.

questions.question: What sign should the elimination row use?
questions.explanation: It offsets the positive post-close target legacy expense.

questions.question: How is new identifiable-intangible amortization calculated?
questions.explanation: The PPA asset is amortized straight-line from the close date.

questions.question: What does Pro Forma Amortization simplify to economically?
options: Olin existing amortization + new PPA amortization
Olin + full target legacy amortization + goodwill amortization
questions.explanation: The visible target add and elimination cancel.

blocks.title: Pro Forma D&A Summary and Links

questions.question: What is Total Pro Forma D&A?
options: Pro Forma Depreciation + Pro Forma Amortization
questions.explanation: The summary combines the two noncash expense categories.

questions.question: What does the consolidated CFS add back?
questions.explanation: The CFS reverses all noncash D&A included in consolidated net income.

questions.question: What should the consolidated income statement subtract separately?
options: Only incremental PPA D&A when legacy D&A is already embedded
questions.explanation: This avoids double-counting legacy D&A.

questions.question: What schedule later rolls the combined PP&E and intangible balances?
options: The consolidated balance sheet / asset roll-forward
questions.explanation: Ongoing asset balances must reflect post-close depreciation and amortization.

modules.title: Synergies & Integration
modules.description: Rebuild the headline synergy assumptions, timing ramps, one-time integration costs, and after-tax impact.

questions.question: Where should headline dollar assumptions live?
questions.explanation: The Main Page is the transaction control panel.

questions.question: What near-term synergy amount is modeled?
questions.explanation: Management disclosed more than $300mm of near-term cost synergies.

questions.question: What additional long-dated benefit is modeled?
questions.explanation: The extra $100mm is separate from the near-term target.

questions.question: What total integration-cost assumption is supported by the disclosed range midpoint?
questions.explanation: The disclosed range is $150mm-$200mm.

questions.question: What near-term ramp is used?
questions.explanation: It matches the disclosed 24-month and year-three realization language.

questions.question: When does the Additional Synergy Ramp reach 100%?
questions.explanation: The long-dated benefit is modeled as beginning in 2031.

questions.question: What must integration-cost timing sum to?
questions.explanation: It allocates a finite total pool.

questions.question: Why are pre-close ramp cells zero?
options: No transaction benefits or costs are recognized before close.
questions.explanation: The schedule follows the assumed close date.

questions.question: How are realized near-term synergies calculated?
questions.explanation: Both achievement and ownership timing matter in the close year.

questions.question: What are approximate 2027 synergies at $300mm, 50%, and 50.4%?
questions.explanation: The three factors multiply to about $75.6mm.

questions.question: What are 2028 synergies at a 95% ramp and full post-close year?
How is Total Realized Synergies calculated?
options: Realized Cost Synergies + Realized Additional Synergies
questions.explanation: The two benefit buckets are added after their separate timing.

questions.question: How are realized integration costs calculated?
options: Positive total cost × post-close period only
questions.explanation: The timing row allocates the full one-time pool and the realized expense is negative.

questions.question: Why should the finite cost pool not be multiplied by Post-Close Period again?
options: The timing percentages already allocate 100% of the total.
It would change the exchange ratio.
questions.explanation: An extra stub factor would leave part of the disclosed cost unmodeled.

questions.question: How is Net Pre-Tax Impact calculated?
options: Total Realized Synergies + Realized Integration Costs
questions.explanation: The cost row is already negative.

questions.question: How is Net Income Impact calculated?
options: Net Pre-Tax Impact + negative Tax Effect
questions.explanation: The tax expense reduces the pre-tax benefit.

modules.title: Pro Forma Financials — Income Statement
modules.description: Rebuild the final full-year pro forma income statement, interest bridge, shares, EPS, and accretion / dilution using the selected Pro Forma Year rather than the legal close-date stub.

questions.question: What should the Full-Year Transaction Factor equal before the selected Pro Forma Year?
questions.explanation: The full-year pro forma presentation is inactive before the year selected in Main Page D14.

questions.question: What should the Full-Year Transaction Factor equal from the selected Pro Forma Year onward?
questions.explanation: From the selected year onward, the full-year pro forma statements assume the transaction is in effect for the entire year.

questions.question: Which date input selects the first full-year pro forma column?
questions.explanation: D14 controls the full-year pro forma presentation; D9 still controls the legal close and opening-balance-sheet date.

questions.question: Should 2027 target earnings be stub-weighted when D14 is 2027?
options: Yes, because the deal closes June 30
No; 2027 is shown as a full-year pro forma period
questions.explanation: The final pro forma statements are a full-year analytical presentation, not the actual GAAP close-year consolidation.

questions.question: How should full-year pro forma Revenue be calculated from the Pro Forma Year onward?
options: Olin Revenue + half of Huntsman Revenue
questions.explanation: The full-year pro forma operating statement combines both standalone businesses for the entire selected year.

questions.question: Why is Target Legacy Amortization Eliminated shown as a positive operating adjustment?
options: It reverses target legacy amortization that purchase accounting replaces
questions.explanation: The target's old finite-lived intangible amortization is eliminated before adding the new PPA amortization.

questions.question: How do negative Realized Integration Costs affect Operating Income?
options: They are added as a signed negative number and reduce Operating Income
They increase EBITDA and Net Income
They are excluded from every earnings measure
questions.explanation: The row already carries a negative sign, so adding it to the operating bridge reduces earnings.

questions.question: What belongs in Incremental PPA D&A on the operating statement?
options: Only new PP&E step-up depreciation and new identifiable-intangible amortization
Total legacy D&A from both companies
questions.explanation: Legacy D&A is already embedded in standalone operating expenses; only transaction-created incremental PPA D&A is a separate adjustment.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Operating Income?
options: Revenue - Total Operating Costs & Expenses + Synergies + Integration Costs + Legacy Amortization Eliminated - Incremental PPA D&A
questions.explanation: Operating Income follows the signed operating bridge and separately reflects PPA and synergy adjustments.

questions.question: What should Stand Alone Interest Expense show before the Pro Forma Year?
questions.explanation: Before the pro forma year, the statements remain Olin standalone.

questions.question: What should Pro Forma Existing Debt Interest reflect from the Pro Forma Year onward?
options: Interest on debt that survives close, using the standalone debt schedules and transaction treatment
The unadjusted sum of both standalone interest lines
A single opening-debt blended rate forever
questions.explanation: The transaction schedule removes repaid facilities and keeps the surviving tranches' year-specific interest.

questions.question: When should Pro Forma New Debt Interest be nonzero?
options: Only when the Debt Financing Switch issues new debt
questions.explanation: New-debt interest depends on actual new financing, not on the existence of the merger itself.

questions.question: Why is Debt Issuance Cost Amortization separate from operating D&A?
options: It is a financing expense tied to debt fees
questions.explanation: Financing-fee amortization belongs below operating income in interest expense.

questions.question: How is Interest Expense, Net calculated in the final pro forma statement?
options: Existing-debt interest + new-debt interest + debt-cost amortization + any interest income
questions.explanation: The line combines all signed financing-income and financing-expense components.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Pre-Tax Income?
options: Operating Income + Interest Expense, Net + Gain / Loss + Other Non-Operating Income / Expense
questions.explanation: All below-the-line items are added using their displayed signs.

questions.question: Under the model's presentation, how is Income Taxes calculated?
questions.explanation: The tax provision is applied to pre-tax income, subject to any separately modeled NOL or cash-tax adjustments.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Standalone Net Income on the pro forma statement?
options: It provides the Olin no-deal earnings comparison used in accretion / dilution
questions.explanation: The standalone earnings line supports the no-deal comparison and EPS bridge.

questions.question: Which earnings figure belongs in the pro forma EPS numerator?
questions.explanation: Public-company EPS uses earnings attributable to the parent company's common shareholders.

questions.question: How is Net Income Attributable to Parent calculated?
options: Net Income - Net Income Attributable to NCI
questions.explanation: The NCI share of earnings is removed from consolidated net income.

questions.question: How should consideration shares be treated in the full-year Pro Forma Year?
options: Include the full consideration share count
Include only the legal close-date fraction
questions.explanation: The full-year pro forma presentation assumes the stock consideration was outstanding for the entire selected year.

questions.question: Should Huntsman's standalone shares be added to Olin's shares?
options: No; Huntsman shares are exchanged and replaced by new Olin consideration shares
questions.explanation: The target shares cease to exist in the exchange.

questions.question: How is Diluted EPS calculated?
options: Net Income Attributable to Parent / Diluted Shares
questions.explanation: EPS uses parent-attributable earnings and the period's diluted weighted-average shares.

questions.question: How is EPS Accretion / Dilution calculated?
options: Pro Forma Diluted EPS / Olin Standalone Diluted EPS - 1
Pro Forma Net Income / Olin Net Income
questions.explanation: Accretion compares EPS, not aggregate net income.

questions.question: Why can an all-stock deal be accretive even though the buyer issues many shares?
options: The target's incremental earnings and synergies can exceed the dilution from the new share count
questions.explanation: Accretion depends on the relationship between incremental earnings and incremental shares.

questions.question: What should the Pro Forma Year Factor Check prove?
options: It is 0 before D14 and 1 from D14 onward
It equals the legal close-date stub in every period
questions.explanation: The check confirms that the full-year pro forma switch is working.

questions.question: What should the Interest Schedule Tie compare?
options: Pro forma interest rows to the full-year outputs of Transaction & Refinancing Debt
questions.explanation: The joint debt schedule is the source of truth for post-transaction interest.

questions.question: What should the Standalone EPS Tie compare?
options: The pro forma statement's Olin Standalone Diluted EPS to Olin Standalone
Pro forma EPS to share price
questions.explanation: The no-deal EPS comparison must link directly to the standalone source.

questions.question: What should the Accretion / Dilution Tie recompute?
questions.explanation: The final output should be independently reproducible from the two EPS rows.

modules.title: Main Page & Assumptions — Final Audit
modules.description: Rebuild the transaction assumptions and headline outputs, then distinguish user inputs, linked calculations, transaction switches, and the final assumptions that still require sourcing.

questions.question: Which company is the accounting acquirer in the model?
questions.explanation: Olin is the accounting acquirer and its standalone shareholders' equity survives the purchase accounting.

questions.question: What does the Transaction Date control?
options: The legal close timing and latest pre-close year-end
The first full-year pro forma summary column only
questions.explanation: The legal close date drives the opening balance sheet and transaction-date mechanics.

questions.question: What does the Pro Forma Year control?
options: The first year shown with full-year combined treatment
questions.explanation: The pro forma year controls the analytical full-year presentation.

questions.question: What does Close Debt Treatment Switch = 1 mean?
options: Selected existing debt is repaid or refinanced at close
questions.explanation: The global switch activates the instrument-level close-treatment toggles.

questions.question: What does Debt Financing Switch = 0 mean in the current all-stock base case?
options: No new transaction debt is issued
questions.explanation: The clean base case uses stock and existing cash without issuing the optional new debt tranches.

questions.question: How is Stock Per Target Share calculated in an exchange-ratio deal?
options: Target Share Price × Target Diluted Shares
questions.explanation: The exchange ratio specifies how many acquirer shares each target share receives.

questions.question: How is Equity Consideration calculated?
options: Offer Price Per Share × Target Diluted Shares
Acquirer Share Price × Acquirer Basic Shares
questions.explanation: The target's fully diluted share count is valued at the offer price.

questions.question: How is Enterprise Value calculated from the transaction consideration?
questions.explanation: Enterprise value bridges from the target equity value to the value of the operating business.

questions.question: Why should Target Net Debt not be added to Total Purchase Consideration in the goodwill calculation?
options: It belongs in the enterprise-value bridge, not consideration transferred for the target equity
It is already a transaction fee
questions.explanation: Purchase accounting begins with consideration transferred to the target equity holders.

questions.question: What should Cash Consideration % plus Stock Consideration % equal?
questions.explanation: The form-of-consideration percentages must account for the entire equity purchase price.

questions.question: What belongs in Debt Refinanced or Repaid?
options: Only debt selected for repayment under the close-treatment switches
The target net-debt figure from valuation
questions.explanation: Sources & Uses should reflect the actual close treatment selected in the joint debt schedule.

questions.question: How are transaction fees treated in Sources & Uses?
options: As a cash use at close
questions.explanation: Transaction fees consume cash and are expensed rather than capitalized into goodwill.

questions.question: How are financing fees treated in Sources & Uses?
options: As a use tied to new financing and later amortized
questions.explanation: Financing fees are paid at close and capitalized as a contra-debt or deferred financing cost.

questions.question: Which formula calculates Total Uses?
options: Sum of all signed use rows
questions.explanation: Every cash and noncash consideration use must be included once.

questions.question: How is Number of Shares issued calculated in the all-stock deal?
questions.explanation: The fixed exchange ratio converts target diluted shares into new Olin consideration shares.

questions.question: How is Value of Shares Issued calculated?
options: Number of Shares × Acquirer Share Price
questions.explanation: The accounting value of the stock consideration is based on the issued share count and the acquirer reference price.

questions.question: What should Existing Cash Used do when stock plus new debt already exceed Total Uses?
options: Never become negative; reduce financing or create an explicit use for the excess
questions.explanation: Negative cash used would hide an overfunded Sources & Uses case.

questions.question: What must the Sources - Uses check equal in the base case?
questions.explanation: A balanced transaction model has equal total sources and total uses.

questions.question: How is Total Purchase Consideration calculated?
questions.explanation: The total is the consideration transferred to acquire the target equity.

questions.question: Should transaction fees be included in New Goodwill?
options: Only when financing fees are zero
questions.explanation: Acquisition-related transaction fees are expensed and excluded from purchase consideration.

questions.question: Where should the detailed New Goodwill calculation live?
questions.explanation: The Main Page should display a linked output rather than duplicate the PPA mechanics.

questions.question: What is the key presentation rule for the Main Page goodwill number?
options: Link to the PPA schedule's output; do not independently recalculate it
Set goodwill equal to target book equity
questions.explanation: One source of truth prevents the headline output from drifting from the detailed schedule.

questions.question: Which assumption drives incremental PP&E step-up depreciation?
questions.explanation: The PP&E step-up is depreciated over its assumed useful life.

questions.question: Which assumption drives new identifiable-intangible amortization?
questions.explanation: Finite-lived transaction intangibles are amortized over the selected life.

questions.question: What is the correct role of Refinancing Rate?
options: It prices refinanced or new debt interest
questions.explanation: The rate is a financing assumption and must never be used as a depreciation or amortization life.

questions.question: Which assumptions remain analytically important to source or clearly label?
options: PPA step-ups, synergy timing, integration costs, tax / NOL treatment, and capital allocation
None; every assumption is disclosed fact
questions.explanation: The remaining work is assumption quality and transparency.

questions.question: Why should the $100mm PP&E step-up and $200mm new-intangible amounts be labeled clearly?
options: They are analyst placeholder PPA assumptions unless supported by a filing or valuation
questions.explanation: The model should never present illustrative fair-value allocations as disclosed facts.

questions.question: What assumption is needed once net debt becomes negative?
questions.explanation: The company must eventually deploy surplus cash through buybacks, dividends, acquisitions, or other uses.

questions.question: How is Amount Issued calculated?
questions.explanation: The switch activates or deactivates each optional new financing tranche.

questions.question: What is the base-case Amount Issued when Debt Financing Switch = 0?
questions.explanation: The current clean all-stock base case does not issue optional transaction debt.

questions.question: How should Annual Fee Amortization be calculated?
options: Allocated financing fees / appropriate debt life
questions.explanation: Capitalized financing fees are amortized over the life of the related debt.

questions.question: Why should this block link to Transaction & Refinancing Debt?
options: The joint debt schedule owns issuance, fees, interest, and debt balances
The Main Page should own all detailed debt mechanics
The PPA schedule owns debt maturities
questions.explanation: The Main Page is a summary and input surface, not a second debt schedule.

questions.question: How is target EV / EBITDA calculated?
questions.explanation: The valuation multiple compares target enterprise value with target EBITDA.

questions.question: Where should the headline pro forma outputs link from?
questions.explanation: The Main Page should display model outputs from the final statements and summary.

questions.question: Why is EPS Accretion / Dilution more decision-useful than Pro Forma Net Income alone?
options: It accounts for both incremental earnings and the new share count
questions.explanation: Shareholders care about earnings per share, not only aggregate earnings.

questions.question: What should negative Net Debt in later years signal on this page?
options: Excess cash accumulation and a missing capital-allocation assumption
A broken tax formula by definition
questions.explanation: The business is modeled to generate surplus cash faster than it deploys it.

modules.title: Pro Forma Financials — Balance Sheet
modules.description: Rebuild the transaction-adjusted opening balance sheet and roll it forward with standalone annual movements, PPA schedules, debt schedules, retained earnings, and CFS ending cash.

blocks.title: Opening Balance and Annual Movement Architecture

questions.question: What is the starting point for the first pro forma forecast year?
options: The Pro Forma Opening Balance Sheet
The sum of the historical subtotal rows
questions.explanation: The opening balance sheet contains the transaction-adjusted starting accounts.

questions.question: How should an ordinary operating account be projected from the opening balance?
options: Opening balance + Olin annual change + Huntsman annual change
Current Olin balance + half the target balance
questions.explanation: The standalone models provide annual movements while the opening balance preserves transaction adjustments.

questions.question: Why is simple current-year standalone addition not universally correct?
options: It can erase opening purchase-accounting, refinancing, or reclassification adjustments
Standalone statements never forecast operating accounts
questions.explanation: Transaction-created opening differences must survive the roll-forward.

questions.question: Should year-end target balance-sheet accounts be time-weighted in the legal close year?
options: No; balance sheets are point-in-time snapshots
questions.explanation: Once the deal has closed, the entire target balance sheet is consolidated at year-end.

questions.question: What should later years use after the first pro forma forecast year?
options: Prior-year pro forma ending balance plus current-year movements
The original opening balance every year
questions.explanation: The combined balance sheet becomes the prior-year starting point.

questions.question: Where should forecast Cash and Cash Equivalents link from?
questions.explanation: The cash flow statement owns the cash roll-forward.

questions.question: What does an increase in Accounts Receivable do to cash flow, all else equal?
questions.explanation: An increase in an operating asset ties up cash.

questions.question: What does an increase in Inventory do to cash flow, all else equal?
questions.explanation: More cash is invested in inventory.

questions.question: How should Total Current Assets be calculated?
options: Sum the adjusted pro forma current-asset line items
Add the two standalone Total Current Assets rows
questions.explanation: Subtotals must be rebuilt from adjusted line items.

questions.question: Why can summing standalone subtotal rows produce a false zero balance-sheet check?
options: The subtotals may omit transaction adjustments that were applied only to underlying accounts
The target has no current assets
questions.explanation: A zero check is meaningful only when every subtotal uses the adjusted pro forma accounts.

blocks.title: PP&E, Goodwill, Intangibles, and Deferred Taxes

questions.question: How should Gross PP&E roll forward?
options: Prior Gross PP&E - negative CFS Capex + disposals / other movements
questions.explanation: Capex is stored as a negative investing cash flow, so subtracting it adds the investment to gross PP&E.

questions.question: How should negative Accumulated Depreciation roll forward?
options: Prior balance - current depreciation + disposal adjustments
questions.explanation: Positive depreciation makes the negative contra-asset more negative.

questions.question: How should Goodwill behave absent impairment or another acquisition?
questions.explanation: Goodwill is not amortized under GAAP.

questions.question: How should new identifiable intangibles roll forward?
options: Opening new intangibles - cumulative new amortization
questions.explanation: Finite-lived intangible assets decline through amortization.

questions.question: How should the incremental deferred-tax liability roll forward?
options: Through the book-versus-cash tax effect of the PPA D&A
questions.explanation: The temporary basis difference reverses as the stepped-up assets are depreciated or amortized.

questions.question: What does an increase in Accounts Payable do to cash flow, all else equal?
questions.explanation: The company is delaying payment to suppliers.

questions.question: What determines Current Portion of Debt?
options: Principal due within the next twelve months
questions.explanation: Debt classification is based on the maturity schedule.

questions.question: Does moving debt from long-term to current create a financing cash flow?
options: No; it is a noncash reclassification
Yes; it is new debt issued
questions.explanation: Cash changes only when principal is issued or repaid.

questions.question: How should Less: Debt Issuance Costs roll forward?
options: Opening contra-debt balance + amortization and any new or written-off fees
questions.explanation: The negative unamortized balance moves toward zero as the fees are amortized.

questions.question: How should Total Liabilities be calculated?
options: From adjusted current liabilities, total long-term debt, deferred taxes, other long-term liabilities, and NCI
By adding standalone Total Liabilities rows only
questions.explanation: The subtotal must use the post-transaction liability accounts.

questions.question: What happens to target historical equity in purchase accounting?
options: It is added to acquirer equity
questions.explanation: The target's historical shareholders' equity does not survive the acquisition.

questions.question: How is new Common Stock recorded for consideration shares?
questions.explanation: Common Stock records par value; APIC receives the residual value.

questions.question: How should Retained Earnings roll forward?
options: Prior Retained Earnings + Parent Net Income + signed Dividends + other adjustments
questions.explanation: Retained earnings accumulates earnings and distributions.

questions.question: What should Common Shares Outstanding include after close?
options: Olin ending shares plus the full consideration shares
Olin shares plus Huntsman old shares
questions.explanation: The point-in-time share count includes all new Olin consideration shares after closing.

questions.question: What should the Assets = Liabilities + Equity Check equal?
questions.explanation: A balanced model has equal total assets and total liabilities plus equity.

questions.question: What should the Cash Tie compare?
options: Balance-sheet cash to CFS Ending Cash
questions.explanation: The balance sheet and cash flow statement must use the same cash balance.

questions.question: What should the Debt Tie compare?
options: Current plus long-term debt to the transaction / debt schedule
questions.explanation: The supporting debt schedule is the source of truth for principal balances.

questions.question: What should the Retained Earnings Tie recompute?
options: Prior RE + parent net income + signed dividends + adjustments
questions.explanation: The equity roll-forward should independently reproduce ending retained earnings.

modules.title: Pro Forma Financials — Cash Flow Statement
modules.description: Rebuild operating, investing, and financing cash flows, roll ending cash into the balance sheet, and calculate free cash flow, net debt, and leverage.

blocks.title: Cash Flow from Operations
rows: Change in Other Operating Assets & Liabilities

questions.question: Where should Net Income at the top of the CFS link from?
questions.explanation: The CFS begins with the same net income produced by the income statement.

questions.question: Why is D&A added back?
options: It reduced earnings but did not use current-period cash
questions.explanation: D&A is a noncash expense.

questions.question: Why is Stock-Based Compensation added back?
options: It is a noncash expense in the period
questions.explanation: The income-statement expense does not consume current-period cash.

questions.question: How is Operating Net Working Capital calculated?
options: Operating current assets excluding cash less operating current liabilities excluding debt
questions.explanation: Operating NWC removes financing accounts such as cash and debt.

questions.question: What is the cash-flow sign when Operating NWC increases?
questions.explanation: More cash is tied up in net operating assets.

questions.question: Why is a gain on an asset sale subtracted in CFO?
options: The gain is included in net income, but the full cash proceeds belong in CFI
The gain is a debt repayment
questions.explanation: The CFS removes the non-operating accounting gain to avoid double counting the sale proceeds.

questions.question: What sign should Capital Expenditures carry on the CFS?
questions.explanation: Capex is an investing cash outflow.

questions.question: Where do full asset-sale proceeds appear?
questions.explanation: The full cash consideration received from the sale is an investing inflow.

questions.question: How should Cash Flow from Investing be calculated?
options: Sum of all signed investing rows
questions.explanation: Each investing activity is included with its cash-flow sign.

questions.question: Does ordinary capex immediately reduce Net Income?
options: No; it is capitalized and depreciated over time
questions.explanation: Capex affects cash and PP&E immediately, while depreciation affects earnings over time.

questions.question: When does debt principal enter the CFS?
options: When it is issued or repaid
questions.explanation: Principal issuance and repayment are financing cash flows.

questions.question: Should a current-versus-long-term debt reclassification enter CFF?
questions.explanation: The reclassification is noncash.

questions.question: Why should net share-count movement not automatically create Stock Issuance cash proceeds?
options: Share movement may reflect SBC, treasury reissuance, retirement, or offsetting activity rather than cash issuance
Every share is always issued for cash
questions.explanation: Cash stock activity requires its own explicit assumption.

questions.question: What sign should Dividends Paid carry?
questions.explanation: Dividends are financing cash outflows.

questions.question: How should Cash Flow from Financing be calculated?
options: Sum of all signed financing rows
questions.explanation: Debt, equity, and dividend cash flows are combined using their signs.

questions.question: How is Net Change in Cash calculated?
questions.explanation: All three cash-flow sections and FX effects combine to produce the period change.

questions.question: What should Beginning Cash equal after the first forecast year?
questions.explanation: Cash rolls forward cumulatively.

questions.question: How is Ending Cash calculated?
options: Beginning Cash + Net Change in Cash
questions.explanation: The cash roll-forward connects the beginning and ending balance-sheet cash accounts.

questions.question: Where should Ending Cash flow?
options: The same-year pro forma balance-sheet Cash line
questions.explanation: The CFS ending balance is the balance-sheet cash source of truth.

blocks.title: EBITDA, Net Debt, Leverage, and Free Cash Flow

questions.question: How is Normalized EBITDA calculated in the model?
options: Normalized EBIT + Total Pro Forma D&A
questions.explanation: EBITDA adds back operating depreciation and amortization to EBIT.

questions.question: How is Net Debt calculated?
questions.explanation: Net debt measures debt after available cash.

questions.question: How is Free Cash Flow calculated in the summary convention?
options: Cash Flow from Operations + negative Capital Expenditures
questions.explanation: With capex stored as a negative number, CFO plus capex yields free cash flow.

questions.question: How is Net Leverage calculated?
questions.explanation: Net leverage compares net borrowings with cash earnings capacity.

questions.question: What does negative Net Debt indicate?
questions.explanation: The company has a net cash position.

modules.title: Summary & Accretion / Dilution
modules.description: Build the dynamic 2027-2031 output table, pull the correct rows with aligned INDEX / MATCH ranges, and present pro forma earnings, accretion, synergies, net debt, and free cash flow.

questions.question: How should the first summary date be calculated?
options: December 31 of the year in Main Page D14
The legal close date in D9
questions.explanation: The summary begins with the selected full-year pro forma period.

questions.question: How should the next summary date be calculated?
questions.explanation: Using real dates keeps the year-header MATCH formulas reliable.

questions.question: What should happen after the 2031 header?
questions.explanation: The summary is capped at the available forecast horizon.

questions.question: Why should a blank guard check the prior header before calling YEAR?
options: YEAR("") can produce a 1900-era date sequence
It prevents INDEX from matching rows
questions.explanation: The guard avoids the 12/31/01, 12/31/02 error pattern.

questions.question: Which source row should Pro Forma Revenue pull?
questions.explanation: The summary label can differ, but the helper lookup must match the actual source row.

questions.question: Which source row should Pro Forma EBITDA pull?
questions.explanation: The detailed statements label the output Normalized EBITDA.

questions.question: Why can Pro Forma Net Income be omitted from a very compact banker summary?
options: EPS already incorporates net income and share dilution
questions.explanation: EPS and accretion often communicate the shareholder impact more directly.

questions.question: What formatting should Pro Forma Diluted EPS use?
options: A per-share number, typically two decimals
questions.explanation: EPS is a currency-per-share output.

questions.question: Which Olin row should the standalone EPS lookup use?
options: Diluted EPS on the pro forma statement
questions.explanation: The no-deal comparison must pull the standalone diluted EPS row.

questions.question: How is EPS Accretion / Dilution calculated?
options: Pro Forma Net Income / Standalone Net Income
questions.explanation: The calculation compares per-share earnings under the transaction and no-deal cases.

questions.question: What does a positive accretion percentage mean?
options: Pro forma EPS exceeds standalone EPS
questions.explanation: Positive accretion means the buyer's shareholders receive higher modeled EPS.

questions.question: Why did tiny values such as 0.035 appear in the standalone EPS row during the build?
options: The INDEX and MATCH ranges were misaligned and returned the wrong worksheet row
questions.explanation: A relative row position from B34:B59 was applied to an INDEX range with a different origin.

questions.question: What should the Accretion / Dilution Recalculation check compare?
options: The displayed percentage to Pro Forma EPS / Standalone EPS - 1
questions.explanation: The key shareholder output should be independently reproducible.

questions.question: How should Gross Debt be calculated for the summary?
options: Current Portion of Debt + gross Long-Term Debt
Total Long-Term Debt after debt issuance costs only
questions.explanation: Gross debt excludes cash and generally excludes the contra-debt issuance-cost balance.

questions.question: How should Net Debt be calculated?
questions.explanation: Cash offsets debt in the net leverage calculation.

questions.question: What should the summary do when Net Debt becomes negative?
options: Show the net cash position and flag the capital-allocation assumption
questions.explanation: Negative net debt is informative but may require an explicit assumption for excess cash deployment.

questions.question: Why is Free Cash Flow useful on the summary?
options: It shows the cash available for debt repayment, dividends, buybacks, or acquisitions
questions.explanation: Free cash flow explains the rapid deleveraging and cash accumulation.

questions.question: Why use a helper row label beside each summary metric?
options: It can exactly match the source-sheet row even when the visible summary label is more polished
questions.explanation: A hidden or adjacent helper label makes generic lookups reusable.

questions.question: What alignment rule must the INDEX value range and source label range follow?
options: They must start and end on corresponding worksheet rows
MATCH must begin seven rows later
The year range must include the label column
questions.explanation: MATCH returns a relative position inside its range.

questions.question: What alignment rule must the INDEX columns and year header range follow?
options: They must begin on corresponding worksheet columns
The header range should start one column earlier
The year MATCH should use row labels
questions.explanation: The column position returned by MATCH must map to the same column inside INDEX.

questions.question: Why can IFERROR be dangerous while building the summary?
options: It can hide misspelled labels and broken date matches
questions.explanation: Use IFERROR only after validating the underlying row and year matches.

questions.question: What should a lookup return for a summary year beyond 2031?
questions.explanation: The summary should end cleanly at the available forecast horizon.
